items.description: The royal palace in Foumban is the seat of the Bamoun kingdom. It remains the city's main symbol of royal tradition.
An old Atlantic slave-trade site near Limbe. The ruins mark one of the darkest chapters in the region's coastal history.
A colonial-era lighthouse on Kribi's coast. It has long guided shipping along the Atlantic shoreline.
An old government residence in Buea linked to Cameroon's colonial and post-colonial administration. It is part of the city's political memory.
A colonial-era fountain in Douala. It is one of the city's oldest surviving monuments from the German period.
The palace of Charles Atangana in Yaounde recalls a major traditional leader from the colonial era. It reflects local power under French rule.
The palace of the Fon of Mankon is a traditional authority center near Bamenda. It remains a key site of Grassfields culture.
The palace of Bafut is one of the best known traditional compounds in northwest Cameroon. It preserves the history of the Bafut chiefdom.
A major Catholic cathedral in Yaounde. It is one of the capital's best-known religious buildings.
A national monument in Yaounde commemorating the reunification of Cameroon in 1961. It is a central symbol of state unity.
A large traditional palace in northern Cameroon and the seat of the Rey Bouba lamidat. It represents enduring Fulani rulership.
A traditional chiefdom in the western highlands. It preserves the political and cultural identity of Bandjoun.
An archaeological site in the Mandara Mountains of far northern Cameroon. The ruins are linked to the early history of the region.
An old colonial cemetery in Douala. It keeps graves and traces from the German period of the city's history.
A French colonial-era monument in Yaounde. It is tied to the city's wartime and administrative past.
